# Results — Study 403 (Hammer & Hanging Man) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — detect the
hammer / hanging-man candle by precise OHLC rules across a fixed basket of **26** liquid US
large-caps + SPY (yfinance **un-adjusted, price-only** daily bars), measure the **forward
1/3/5/10-day return** entered at the **next close** (one execution lag) against each name's
**unconditional base rate**, and run a HAC one-sample *t* + a label-shuffle placebo. As-of
**2026-06-23**. Pooled across the basket; the same candle shape is split by **prior trend**
into the bullish **hammer** (after a downtrend) and the bearish **hanging man** (after an
uptrend).*

## Data stamp

- **Basket** (26, survivors): SPY, AAPL, MSFT, JNJ, PG, KO, JPM, WMT, XOM, CVX, PFE, MRK,
  INTC, CSCO, HD, MCD, DIS, BA, CAT, MMM, HON, UNH, ORCL, PEP, COST, GS.
- **Span**: 1962-01-02 → 2026-06-23 · **345,716** daily bars · **11,816** hammer-shaped bars.
- **Adjustment**: un-adjusted OHLC (the candle *shape* needs the printed levels); forward
  returns are therefore **price-only** (no dividends).
- **Content fingerprint** (close columns over the basket): `d488237f4299`.
- **Survivorship**: a fixed surviving-names basket — the bias points *toward* finding a
  post-dip bounce (survivors recover from dips that delisted names did not), so a null/weak
  hammer result is **conservative**. Named on the Signal axis.

## The bullish claim — HAMMER (shape after a downtrend), gross & net

The folk recipe: a long lower wick after a slide marks a floor — buy it. Edge = conditional
mean minus that name's base rate; net = gross − 2 × 5 bps round trip (long-only, no borrow).

| Horizon | n | cond % | base % | **edge %** | win % | **HAC *t*** | placebo *p* | net % |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day  | 5,152 | +0.028 | +0.066 | **−0.031** | 48.0 | **−0.82** | 0.869 | −0.131 |
| 3 days | 5,149 | +0.227 | +0.196 | **+0.052** | 51.0 | **+0.92** | 0.128 | −0.048 |
| 5 days | 5,148 | +0.333 | +0.325 | **+0.043** | 52.0 | **+0.63** | 0.241 | −0.057 |
| 10 days| 5,144 | +0.595 | +0.640 | **+0.023** | 53.5 | **+0.23** | 0.383 | −0.077 |

- The hammer's best edge is **+0.05% over 3 days at HAC *t* = +0.92** — nowhere near the
  **t ≥ 2** bar, and the placebo *p* = 0.13 says a random sort of the same days clears it
  one time in eight. **No real bullish floor.**
- At 1 day the edge is *negative* (−0.03%, *t* = −0.82): the hammer's own first-day move
  slightly *underperforms* the name.
- **Net of costs the edge is negative at every horizon** (−0.05% to −0.13%): a tiny gross
  blip the round trip eats whole.

## The bearish claim — HANGING MAN (same shape after an uptrend)

| Horizon | n | cond % | base % | edge % | win % | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net % |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day  | 6,493 | +0.022 | +0.066 | −0.037 | 48.1 | −1.71 | 0.942 | −0.137 |
| 3 days | 6,493 | +0.079 | +0.196 | **−0.099** | 50.3 | **−2.63** | 0.993 | −0.199 |
| 5 days | 6,492 | +0.195 | +0.325 | −0.098 | 51.2 | −2.02 | 0.977 | −0.198 |
| 10 days| 6,489 | +0.507 | +0.640 | −0.072 | 53.4 | −1.00 | 0.852 | −0.172 |

The same shape after an *uptrend* does **underperform** (3-day edge −0.10%, *t* = −2.63) —
a statistically real *negative* tilt, consistent with the bearish-reversal direction. But it
is **+0.08% absolute** (the stock still rises, just less than its drift), and a long-only
buyer of the hammer can't harvest it; shorted, it's eaten by costs (net −0.20%). The candle
carries a faint "lower-than-usual return" signal, not a tradable floor or a tradable top.

## The shape alone — ANY (ignoring trend)

| Horizon | n | edge % | HAC *t* | net % |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 / 3 / 5 / 10 day | 11,816 | −0.032 / −0.028 / −0.033 / −0.030 | −1.67 / −0.87 / −0.82 / −0.50 | ≈ −0.13 |

Ignore the trend and the long-lower-wick bar simply earns **a hair less** than the
unconditional base rate at every horizon. No directional edge in either direction.

## Myth-check — does a trend / wick filter rescue the hammer? (3-day edge)

| Variant | edge % | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| plain hammer (trend lookback = 10) | +0.052 | +0.92 | 0.128 | 5,149 |
| trend lookback = 5  | +0.095 | **+1.94** | 0.012 | 5,534 |
| trend lookback = 20 | −0.017 | −0.34 | 0.637 | 4,973 |
| stricter wick (≥ 3× body) | +0.005 | +0.07 | 0.478 | 2,510 |
| stricter wick (≥ 4× body) | +0.005 | +0.05 | 0.486 | 1,419 |

The folk "add a filter" rescue is a **snoop**: a *shorter* trend window (lookback = 5) lifts
*t* to **1.94** — tantalisingly close but still under the bar — while a *longer* one
(lookback = 20) sends it back to zero, and demanding a *longer, purer* wick (the "better
hammer") **kills the edge entirely** (*t* ≈ 0.05). The signal you can dial in by choosing the
filter is the signature of a mirage, not an effect.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's a floor to find

On a deterministic OHLC panel (`data.synthetic_panel`) where we **plant** a post-hammer
bounce, the same engine reads ≈ 0 with no edge and lights up when one exists:

| planted bounce | events | edge % | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | win % |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.000 (random walk) | 2,415 | +0.005 | +0.22 | 0.403 | 49.9 |
| 0.005 (real floor)  | 2,423 | +0.324 | **+13.45** | 0.000 | 61.4 |

Zero edge cannot fake significance (*t* = 0.22); a genuine 0.5%/event floor is detected at
*t* = 13.5. So the flat real-tape *t* is a true negative, not a blind harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The bullish hammer never clears the bar: best edge **+0.05% at 3 days,
  HAC *t* = +0.92** (placebo *p* = 0.13), and *negative* at the 1-day horizon. The only "real"
  statistic is the hanging man's faint *under*-performance (3-day *t* = −2.63) — the wrong
  sign for a floor, and untradeable. The harness detects a planted floor at *t* = 13.5, so
  the flat reading is genuine. Survivorship tilts *toward* a bounce, making this conservative.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of a 5-bps round trip the edge is **negative at every
  horizon and on every side** (−0.05% to −0.20%). There is no positive gross edge to defend.
- **Reliable reversal? — BUSTED.** The same shape doesn't mark a floor (hammer) or a top you
  can short (hanging man); the only way to nudge *t* upward is to snoop the trend window, and
  a *longer/purer* wick — the "stronger" signal the folklore prizes — makes it *worse*.
